Hi Samir — great to meet you.

Short answer: we can sometimes provide a temporary invoice-only path for pilots under $5k but it needs an approved exception and a few safeguards on record. Typical ask from our side: W-9 (or local tax form), basic SOC attestations if the pilot will host customer data (not required for a pure eval), and an owner-approved temporary agreement that limits spend and duration.

I've looped in Marissa (rev ops) and Vanessa (procurement lead) to confirm what documentation procurement will accept for a 30-day pilot. In parallel, can you send the W-9 and a primary contact for billing? If procurement is comfortable we can spin this up quickly.

Proposed next step: I’ll draft a short temporary no-PO agreement that locks the pilot to $4,500 and 30 days; we'll capture billing contact and require a credit card or ACH on file as a fallback. Does that work?

Thanks,
Priyom

Folks — quick procurement POV.

We can approve a timeboxed invoice-only path for small pilots but require:
- W-9 (or VAT form for non-US entities)
- Company registration (incorporation docs) and a POA for payment contact
- Spend limit enforced in our billing system ($4,500 max)
- Pre-approved fallback: card/ACH on file or retention of final invoice with 14-day payment SLA
- Completed vendor onboarding form (I’ll accept the short intake)

Risk controls: proof of commercial liability insurance is preferred but not mandatory for trials < $5k. For any pilot that will store customer data, we need a short security attestation — otherwise we mark it as no-customer-data pilot.

I uploaded a short risk matrix template and our vendor intake stub in Drive. If legal agrees, we can sign a 1-page temporary exception (I suggested language below).

Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference

Hi Vanessa / Priyom,

Thanks for the heads-up. To record MicroVendor as invoice-only for 30 days, we need:
1) Completed vendor intake form (fields: legal name, tax id, remittance address, bill-to contact)
2) W-9 (or equivalent) attached to the intake
3) Point-of-contact for billing and a backup
4) Bank details for ACH (optional if card on file)
5) Any customer-data handling flags (Y/N) + brief attestation if yes

Once we receive the intake + W-9, procurement will issue an internal exception record and set the spend cap in the billing system. If legal wants the temporary exception signed, route to legal@redwood.ai and we’ll hold off on activation until signed.

Regards,
ProcureOps Intake Team
